svg.title: Thread per task vs thread pool
svg.desc: Left, thread per task: 10,000 requests create 10,000 threads. About 1 MB stack each, so about 10 GB reserved; a thread is created and destroyed for every task; the CPU is busy context-switching; it ends in OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread. Right, thread pool: incoming tasks go into a bounded queue and 4 workers (worker-1 to worker-4) take tasks from it and are reused. Threads are created once, then reused; the queue absorbs bursts; a bounded queue gives backpressure or rejection when full; concurrency is capped.
